CHART CODE
 import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd

data = {
    'Intervention': [
        'Risk Mapping', 'Community Education', 'School Reintegration',
        'Vocational Training', 'Legal Advocacy', 'Corporate Audits',
        'Local Policy Reform', 'Health Programs', 'Child Protection Panels',
        'Agricultural Certification', 'Supply Chain Tracking', 'Social Safety Net',
        'Awareness Campaigns', 'Worker Cooperatives', 'Digital Monitoring',
        'Community Policing', 'Parental Support', 'Microfinance Loans'
    ],
    'Cases Prevented': [
        1850, 2400, 3420, 4870, 5230, 4100, 3980, 2760,
        3150, 6740, 8250, 7410, 2980, 5320, 6590, 2050, 3600, 4200
    ],
    'Effectiveness Score': [
        65, 75, 85, 92, 88, 78, 81, 69,
        76, 95, 97, 93, 70, 91, 94, 68, 79, 83
    ],
    'Cost per Intervention (USD)': [
        15000, 22000, 38000, 55000, 62000, 48000, 45000, 28000,
        35000, 85000, 110000, 92000, 30000, 65000, 88000, 18000, 40000, 47000
    ],
    'Sustainability Rating': [
        5, 6, 8, 9, 7, 8, 9, 6,
        7, 10, 9, 8, 5, 9, 10, 6, 8, 7
    ]
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.set_style("whitegrid")
sns.set_palette("husl")

bubble = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='Effectiveness Score',
    y='Cases Prevented',
    size='Cost per Intervention (USD)',
    hue='Sustainability Rating',
    sizes=(100, 2000),
    alpha=0.7,
    edgecolor='w',
    linewidth=0.5
)

plt.title('Effectiveness and Impact of Anti-Child Labor Interventions', fontsize=16, pad=20)
plt.xlabel('Effectiveness Score (1-100)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Child Labor Cases Prevented', fontsize=12)

plt.legend(
    bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1),
    loc='upper left',
    title='Sustainability\nRating (1-10)',
    borderaxespad=0,
    labelspacing=1.2
)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
SUMMARY
 This image is a bubble chart titled "Effectiveness and Impact of Anti-Child Labor Interventions," which visually represents the relationship between various interventions aimed at preventing child labor. The horizontal axis, labeled "Effectiveness Score (1-100)," ranges from 65 to 97, while the vertical axis, labeled "Child Labor Cases Prevented," spans from 2,000 to 8,500 cases.

Each bubble on the chart corresponds to a specific intervention, with its position determined by the effectiveness score and the number of child labor cases prevented. The size of each bubble indicates the cost per intervention in USD, with larger bubbles representing more expensive interventions and smaller bubbles representing less costly ones. The bubbles vary significantly in size, reflecting a broad range of intervention costs.

The color of each bubble represents the sustainability rating of the intervention, using a gradient scale from lighter to darker shades of purple. The sustainability rating ranges from 5 to 10, with lighter colors indicating lower ratings and darker colors reflecting higher ratings. A legend on the right side of the chart clarifies these color codes and bubble sizes for better interpretation.

Notably, the interventions with the highest effectiveness scores (above 90) tend to prevent the most child labor cases, often exceeding 6,000. These interventions also tend to have higher sustainability ratings and larger costs, as indicated by the darker colors and bigger bubble sizes. Conversely, interventions with lower effectiveness scores and fewer cases prevented generally have smaller bubbles and lighter colors, suggesting lower costs and sustainability ratings. This visualization effectively highlights the trade-offs between cost, effectiveness, and long-term sustainability of anti-child labor interventions.
